mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative response to rate hikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects diminish.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative response to unemployment rate spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of periods with declining GDP, or 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative response to GDP declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive response to industrial production increases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and CPI inflation exceeds 3% year-over-year, the combination signals a high inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative response to the combined high inflation and high rates environment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 300,000 in a month and the unemployment rate simultaneously decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market with falling unemployment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300k in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.3%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 5-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive response to strong labor market signals (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing sector is a key component of economic demand and growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative response to housing starts declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of periods with increasing consumption, or 5-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive response to consumption increases (t-test p > 0.05).
